name: X Utility
description: An open-source, cross-platform toolbox for installing software and managing your system from one clean interface.

features.title: Cross-platform installation
features.description: One catalog of tools that adapts to Windows, Linux and macOS using the right package manager for each system.

features.title: Software management
features.description: Browse, search, preview and run installation tasks from a terminal interface or a modern graphical window.

features.title: Linux utilities
features.description: Package managers, system cleanup, firewall checks, SSH setup, printer drivers and self-update tasks.

features.title: Windows utilities
features.description: winget, Chocolatey and Scoop installs, Defender scans, restore points, Explorer tweaks and maintenance tasks.

features.title: macOS utilities
features.description: Homebrew-based app installs and platform-aware catalog entries for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.

features.title: Clean, approachable interface
features.description: Keyboard-first terminal UI and a polished GUI with themes, search, previews and a task queue.

features.title: Open source
features.description: Readable Python source, a TOML catalog you can extend, and a public repository for issues and contributions.

features.title: Lightweight
features.description: The engine uses only the Python standard library. The single-file build carries the whole catalog with no runtime dependencies.

windows: Download the .exe or .msi installer and double-click it.
If SmartScreen warns you, choose More info, then Run anyway.
For the portable build, extract the .zip and run xutil.exe from the folder.
Right-click the app and choose Run as administrator for system-level tasks.
linux: Arch: install from the AUR package or run python3 xutil.py from source.
Universal: python3 xutil.py --gui, or use the single-file dist/xutil.py.
macos: Open the .dmg and drag X Utility to Applications.
For Apple Silicon and Intel builds, pick the matching asset on the release page.
If macOS blocks the app, open System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway.
Homebrew is required for the macOS software catalog.

roadmap.title: Signed release artifacts
roadmap.description: Code-signed installers and published checksums for every platform.

roadmap.title: Plugin catalog
roadmap.description: Community-maintained task packs distributed as separate TOML catalogs.

roadmap.title: Package manager integrations
roadmap.description: First-class winget, apt/dnf/pacman and Homebrew sync status.

roadmap.title: Desktop integrations
roadmap.description: System tray, updater and deeper desktop environment theming.
